arxiv-2012-09702.title: SRoll3: A neural network approach to reduce large-scale systematic effects in the Planck High Frequency Instrument maps
arxiv-2012-09702.creator: G. Wuchterl, C. Ptolemy ,, M. Lopez-Radcenco ,, J.-M. Delouis, L. Vibert
arxiv-2012-09702.description: Abstract In the present work, we propose a neural network based data inversion approach to reduce structured contamination sources, with a particular focus on the mapmaking for Planck High Frequency Instrument data and the removal of large-scale systematic effects within the produced sky maps.

arxiv-2101-02885.title: A unified description of the structure and electromagnetic breakup of 11 Be
arxiv-2101-02885.creator: M. Dan, R. Chatterjee, M. Kimura
arxiv-2101-02885.description: Abstract We study both the static properties of 11 Be and its reaction dynamics during electromagnetic breakup under a unified framework. A many-body approach - the antisymmetrized molecular dynamics (AMD) is used to describe the structure of the neutron-halo nucleus, 11 Be.

arxiv-2104-08374.title: Data-driven Chaos Indicator for Nonlinear Dynamics and Applications on Storage Ring Lattice Design
arxiv-2104-08374.creator: Yongjun Li, Jinyu Wan, Allen Liu, Yi Jiao, Robert Rainer
arxiv-2104-08374.description: Abstract A data-driven chaos indicator concept is introduced to characterize the degree of chaos for nonlinear dynamical systems. The indicator is represented by the prediction accuracy of surrogate models established purely from data. It provides a metric for the predictability of nonlinear motions in a given system.

arxiv-2204-02447.title: Aperiodic subshifts of finite type on groups which are not finitely generated
arxiv-2204-02447.creator: Sebastián Barbieri
arxiv-2204-02447.description: Abstract We provide an example of a non-finitely generated group which admits a nonempty strongly aperiodic SFT. Furthermore, we completely characterize the groups with this property in terms of their finitely generated subgroups and the roots of their conjugacy classes. Keywords: symbolic dynamics, subshift of finite type, aperiodicity. MSC2020: 37B10.

arxiv-2207-04334.title: Polyhedral Estimation of ℒ 1 \mathcal{L}_{1} and ℒ ∞ \mathcal{L}_{\infty} Incremental Gains of Nonlinear Systems Note: This work was supported by the Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council (EPSRC) of the United Kingdom - Project Reference 1950140.
arxiv-2207-04334.creator: Dimitris Kousoulidis, Fulvio Forni
arxiv-2207-04334.description: Abstract We provide novel dissipativity conditions for bounding the incremental ℒ 1 \mathcal{L}_{1} gain of systems. Moreover, we adapt existing results on the ℒ ∞ \mathcal{L}_{\infty} gain to the incremental setting and relate the incremental ℒ 1 \mathcal{L}_{1} and ℒ ∞ \mathcal{L}_{\infty} gain bounds through system adjoints.

arxiv-2303-07381.title: LRG-BEASTS: Evidence for clouds in the transmission spectrum of HATS-46 b 2023 LRG-BEASTS: Evidence for clouds in the transmission spectrum of HATS-46 b – 7
arxiv-2303-07381.creator: E. Ahrer, P. J. Wheatley, S. Gandhi, J. Kirk, G. W. King, T. Louden, L. Welbanks
arxiv-2303-07381.description: Abstract We have performed low-resolution ground-based spectroscopy of HATS-46 b in transmission, using the EFOSC2 instrument on the ESO New Technology Telescope (NTT). HATS-46 b is a highly-inflated exoplanet that is a prime target for transmission spectroscopy, having a Jupiter-like radius (0.95 R Jup {}_{\textrm{Jup}} ) but a much lower mass (0.16 M Jup {}_{\textrm{Jup}} ).

arxiv-2310-18297.title: Image Clustering Conditioned on Text Criteria
arxiv-2310-18297.creator: Sehyun Kwon, Jaeseung Park, Minkyu Kim, Jaewoong Cho, Ernest K. Ryu, Kangwook Lee, Seoul National University, KRAFTON, University of Wisconsin–Madison, Co-senior authors
arxiv-2310-18297.description: Abstract Classical clustering methods do not provide users with direct control of the clustering results, and the clustering results may not be consistent with the relevant criterion that a user has in mind. In this work, we present a new methodology for performing image clustering based on user-specified text criteria by leveraging modern vision-language models and large language models.

arxiv-2411-04005.title: Object-Centric Dexterous Manipulation from Human Motion Data
arxiv-2411-04005.creator: Yuanpei Chen, Chen Wang, Yaodong Yang, C. Karen Liu
arxiv-2411-04005.description: Abstract Manipulating objects to achieve desired goal states is a basic but important skill for dexterous manipulation. Human hand motions demonstrate proficient manipulation capability, providing valuable data for training robots with multi-finger hands. Despite this potential, substantial challenges arise due to the embodiment gap between human and robot hands.

arxiv-2601-09656.title: Connection of hypocoercivity and hypocontractivity via the Cayley transform
arxiv-2601-09656.creator: A. Arnold, S. Egger, V. Mehrmann, E.A. Nigsch
arxiv-2601-09656.description: Abstract The concepts of hypocoercivity and hypocontractivity and their relationship are studied for semi-dissipative continuous-time and discrete-time evolution equations in a Hilbert space setting. New proofs for the characterization of the short-time decay of the solution from the initial value are presented, that in particular characterize the constants in the leading terms of the solution when expanded in time.

pmc-10613247.title: Physical aspects of electro osmotically interactive Cilia propulsion on symmetric plus asymmetric conduit flow of couple stress fluid with thermal radiation and heat transfer
pmc-10613247.creator: Noreen Sher Akbar, Taseer Muhammad
pmc-10613247.description: A novel mathematical analysis is established that summits the key features of Cilia propulsion for a non-Newtonian Couple Stress fluid with the electroosmosis and heat transfer. In such physiological models, the conduit may have a symmetric or asymmetric configuration in accordance with the biological problem.

pmc-11396826.title: Climate Change Impacts on and Response Strategies for Kiwifruit Production: A Comprehensive Review
pmc-11396826.creator: Priyanka Rajan, Premkumar Natraj, Misun Kim, Mockhee Lee, Yeon Jin Jang, Young Jae Lee, Seong Cheol Kim
pmc-11396826.description: Climate change, a pressing global concern, poses significant challenges to agricultural systems worldwide. Among the myriad impacts of climate change, the cultivation of kiwifruit trees (Actinidia spp.) faces multifaceted challenges. In this review, we delve into the intricate effects of climate change on kiwifruit production, which span phenological shifts, distributional changes, physiological responses, and ecological interactions.

pmc-11451040.title: Effective community-based interventions to prevent and control infectious diseases in urban informal settlements in low- and middle-income countries: a systematic review
pmc-11451040.creator: Sohana Shafique, Dipika Shankar Bhattacharyya, Iffat Nowrin, Foyjunnaher Sultana, Md Rayhanul Islam, Goutam Kumar Dutta, Mariam Otmani del Barrio, Daniel D. Reidpath
pmc-11451040.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundThe impact of rapid urbanization taking place across the world is posing variegated challenges. Especially in terms of communicable disease, the risk is more concentrated in urban poor areas where basic amenities are inadequate. This systematic review synthesizes evidence on the effective community-based interventions (CBIs) aimed at preventing and controlling infectious diseases among the urban poor in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs).MethodsThis systematic review was conducted following the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analysis) guidelines.

pmc-11507152.title: Harmonizing Innovations: An In-Depth Comparative Review on the Formulation, Applications, and Future Perspectives of Aerogels and Hydrogels in Pharmaceutical Sciences
pmc-11507152.creator: Nour Alhuda Alaghawani, Hala Alkhatib, Layla Elmancy, Anis Daou
pmc-11507152.description: Gels, specifically hydrogels and aerogels, have emerged as versatile materials with profound implications in pharmaceutical sciences. This comprehensive review looks into detail at hydrogels and aerogels, providing a general introduction to gels as a foundation. The paper is then divided into distinct sections for hydrogels and aerogels, each delving into their unique formulations, advantages, disadvantages, and applications.

pmc-11600718.title: Procyanidin C1 ameliorates acidic pH stress induced nucleus pulposus degeneration through SIRT3/FOXO3-mediated mitochondrial dynamics
pmc-11600718.creator: Wenbin Hua, Lin Xie, Chenpeng Dong, Guoyu Yang, Shouyuan Chi, Zhiqiang Xu, Cao Yang, Huiwen Wang, Xinghuo Wu
pmc-11600718.description: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) is a common cause of low back pain. Procyanidin C1 (PCC1) has been demonstrated to exert a protective effect on nucleus pulposus (NP) cells, and therefore, plays a critical role in the prevention and therapy of IVDD. Clarifying the pathophysiological characteristics and molecular mechanisms of IVDD may be helpful in establishing novel preventive and therapeutic strategies.

pmc-12609321.title: Vitamin D Receptor rs7975232 (ApaI) Variant, Inflammatory Markers, and Patient-Reported Outcomes in Orthopedic Surgery
pmc-12609321.creator: Dariusz Larysz, Remigiusz Recław, Aleksandra Suchanecka, Wojciech Dziurawiec, Rafał Tkacz, Aleksandra Strońska-Pluta, Krzysztof Chmielowiec, Anna Grzywacz, Jolanta Chmielowiec, Jing Cao, Xin Yi
pmc-12609321.description: Background: Genetic variability in the vitamin D receptor (VDR) may influence immune regulation and systemic inflammation, factors potentially relevant for outcomes in orthopedic surgery. This study explored the association of the VDR rs7975232 (ApaI) single nucleotide variation (SNV) with inflammatory biomarkers and health-related quality of life (HRQoL). Methods: The study included 292 orthopedic patients and 90 controls.

pmc-13386047.title: Intrathecal morphine for postoperative analgesia in major laparoscopic abdominal surgery (IMPACT-Scope): a protocol for a randomised controlled trial
pmc-13386047.creator: Wudi Ma, Ciro Morgese, Wei Xiong, Yuxiao Liu, Jinyu Wu, Qiulan He, Ming Wei, Jiangtao Zhou, Ruiming Liang, Natalie Ives, Fangzhou Xu, Louise Jackson, Matthew Soden, Kar Keung Cheng, Fang Gao Smith, Xia Feng
pmc-13386047.description: IntroductionEffective perioperative pain management is a cornerstone of Enhanced Recovery After Surgery, yet standard opioid-based intravenous patient-controlled analgesia often leads to insufficient pain control, excessive adverse reactions and delayed recovery following laparoscopic abdominal surgery. Intrathecal morphine (ITM) has shown promising analgesic efficacy in abdominal and obstetric procedures but high-quality evidence supporting its use in major laparoscopic surgery remains limited.
